title: Devices and the Device contract
tasks: Device(ABC): abstract state() and execute(), plus a concrete describe() every subclass inherits
Light(Device): a 0-100 level with turn_on, turn_off, set_level, and execute for on / off / dim
FACTORIES, build_devices(specs) and devices: build objects by looking classes up in a dict
snapshot() and command(): the two functions the scene calls, which never raise
explanation: The ABC turns the contract into something Python enforces: you cannot create a Device, or a subclass that forgets part of the contract. describe() is written once in the base class and relies on each subclass's state(). FACTORIES maps a Kind to a class, so adding a device type later is one dictionary entry. command() is the boundary: it converts ValueErrors into an error dict so the dashboard never sees a traceback.

hints.title: The base class
hints.content: class Device(ABC): put @abstractmethod above def state(self) and def execute(self, action, value=None). __init__ stores self.spec = spec. describe() returns {"id": self.id, "kind": self.spec.kind.value, "room": self.room.value, **self.state()}.

hints.title: The light
hints.content: Call super().__init__(spec) then set self.level = 0. execute() is an if/elif chain on action: "on" calls turn_on(), "off" calls turn_off(), "dim" calls set_level(value), and else raises UnsupportedAction(f"{self.id} cannot {action!r}"). set_level converts with _number(level, "light level"), checks 0 <= n <= 100, and stores round(n).

hints.title: Factory and boundary
hints.content: FACTORIES = {Kind.LIGHT: Light}. build_devices returns {spec.id: FACTORIES[spec.kind](spec) for spec in specs if spec.kind in FACTORIES}. command() looks the device up with devices.get(device_id), returns an error dict if it is None, then wraps device.execute(action, value) in try/except ValueError.

checks.prompt: You write `class Dimmer(Device)` and forget to implement `execute()`. When does Python complain?

options: Never: abstract methods are only a convention

checks.explanation: Abstract methods are enforced at instantiation: `Dimmer(spec)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` and names the missing method. Defining the class is allowed, which is what lets you build a chain of partly-abstract helper classes.

checks.prompt: `describe()` is defined once on `Device` but returns different data for a `Light` and a `DoorLock`. What makes that work?

options: describe() is copied into each subclass
describe() calls self.state(), which each subclass implements differently
Python picks the data based on the class name
describe() uses isinstance() to check the type

checks.explanation: This is the template-method idea. The base class fixes the shared skeleton (identity first, state after) and delegates the varying part to an abstract method. `self.state()` runs the *subclass's* version because `self` is the real object.
